summary: Pamela Gutman was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna and was a research student at the Australian National University from circa 1971 to 1976.

Pandurang Vaman Kane, an Indologist and historian, studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949) and National Professor of Indology for the Government of India (~1959–1972).
Pankaj Tandon is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under mentor Tom Mallon-McCorgray. He held a post at Boston University, attested in 2015.

Paolo Visigalli is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Padua, the University of Rome (~2007–2010), and the University of Cambridge (~2010–2014), and held a post at New York University Shanghai circa 2018.

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Director of the Mithila Institute (~1954–1958) and succeeded Shripad Krishna Belvalkar in 1961 as General Editor of the Mahabharata at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1961–1972).

Parimal G. Patil specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1993–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–2002), and became a professor at Harvard University circa 2004.

Parul Dave-Mukherji works in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and was a professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

Pasang Wangdu is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under the supervision of Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner. He held a professorship at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006–2014).

Pascale Haag specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and Marie-Claire Gay at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (until 2002) and Paris Nanterre University (until 2018), and held a post at the EHESS circa 2006.

Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), the University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, and held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, studying under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman, and held posts as Curator at the Asian Art Museum and art history faculty at UC Berkeley (1996).

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1982), the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas, where she taught (~1983–1990), before serving as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1991–2018).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani works in Sinology and Tibetology. She studied at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under doctoral supervisor Perry Link.

Patrick Arthur Pranke is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the doctoral supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.

Patrick Jory specializes in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Craig J. Reynolds by 1996 and held a post at the University of Queensland (attested 2016).

Patrick McAllister works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011), studying under Helmut Krasser, Karin Preisendanz, and Ernst Steinkellner, and became a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences circa 2012.

Patrick Olivelle specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Oxford under Gombrich, Burrow, and Zaehner, and earned a Ph.D. at Penn under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (1991).
